title: Prefetch topology optimizer and safeguard for KV/prefix caching
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build an automated prefetch/topology optimizer for KV/prefix caching that recommends TTLs, prefetch buckets, and conservative apply/rollback sequences. The optimizer should produce actionable config diffs (policy + ttl + keying) and a guarded rollout plan: shadow evaluation, metric delta gating, staged canaries, and deterministic rollback. This ticket covers model design, simulator experiments, safe-apply orchestration, observability hooks, and an initial route-level rollout for a subset of customers.
background_and_rationale: Existing prefix-ttl tuning is largely manual and brittle: PMs and SREs create ad-hoc policies that either under-cache (higher token cost) or over-cache (eviction pressure, stale results). We need automated heuristics that infer hit-rate elasticity across prefixes and recommend conservative prefetch shapes. Key research questions: how to measure prefix-level marginal hit uplift; how to safely apply multi-parameter policies (TTL, prefetch window, key canonicalization) without cross-traffic regressions; and which safety gates to make non-bypassable in the orchestration engine.
design_summary: 1) Hit-rate estimator: time-decayed sampling + per-prefix Bayesian shrinkage to estimate baseline and uplift with confidence bands. 2) Topology optimizer: group prefixes into "segments" by access shape (long-tail vs bursty) and assign one of a small set of policy archetypes (conservative, opportunistic, prefetch-ahead). 3) TTL composer: integer TTL proposals with a per-prefix risk score and cost delta estimate (tokens saved vs cache-memory cost). 4) Safe apply: generate an atomic change bundle plus a staged rollout plan (shadow, 1% route canary, 10% route canary, 100% route) with automatic rollback when gating metrics exceed thresholds. 5) Observability: include delta metrics (cost/token, latency P95, cache hit-rate) and synthetic traffic validators.
acceptance_criteria: Hit-rate estimator can produce per-prefix baseline and uplift with 95% CI on historical traces (validated on 2 weeks of production telemetry)
Optimizer emits deterministic config bundles (policy + TTL + key canonicalization) and cost delta estimate for a test workload
Orchestration engine can execute a staged rollout (shadow -> 1% -> 10% -> 100%) with automatic stop/revert if any gating metric breach is detected
Dashboards show per-route delta cost and hit-rate and alert on regressions; on-call runbook updated
Runbook and automated rollback procedure tested in a dry-run (shadow apply) and a small live canary with no customer-visible regressions

decision_log: 2026-02-18: Chose Bayesian shrinkage for per-prefix estimates instead of pure ML model to keep interpretability and low compute
2026-02-21: Use a small set of policy archetypes to limit action space (helps safety and explanation to customers)
2026-02-25: Implement conservative default gating thresholds: cost increase tolerance 3%, latency P95 10% relative increase, hit-rate drop 5% absolute
2026-03-02: Decided to perform key-canonicalization recommendations as a separate optional diff to avoid coupling with TTL changes during initial rollout
tradeoffs_and_risks: Aggressive TTL increases reduce token cost but can increase memory pressure and evictions for multi-tenant workloads
Prefetch introduces extra compute and potential overfetch at headroom; mis-calibrated prefetch windows can worsen tail latency under bursty traffic
Automated apply increases blast radius if gating metrics are insufficiently sensitive; conservative gates reduce potential savings
Estimators rely on sampling; very low-traffic prefixes will have high uncertainty and must be folded into a conservative group
rollback_procedure: Automatic: orchestration reverts to previous config bundle when gating metric breach persists for 3 consecutive measurement windows
Manual: run 'config rollback ENG-924681' playbook to revert and pin previous TTLs and disable optimizer for affected routes
Postmortem: capture pre/post snapshots, include delta metrics and generate RCA within 72 hours
observability_items: Per-prefix hit-rate time-series with confidence bands
Cost delta per route and per 1000 requests
Latency P50/P95/P99 annotated with rollout percentage
Shadow vs live difference charts for gating metrics
Simulation dashboard: predicted vs actual during canaries
experiments_and_results: Synthetic spike test (2026-02-27): conservative prefetch reduced token cost by 9% with no observed latency degradation under 2x baseline traffic
Memory pressure sim (2026-03-05): opportunistic archetype increased eviction rate by 18% on dense-tenant topology — will restrict archetype to single-tenant routes for now
Shadow run (2026-03-09): TTL composer predictions aligned to actual hit uplift within 12% median error across top 500 prefixes
